brief: The S&P 500 has fallen 12% from its October 6 high, exceeding the median historical correction magnitude; Goldman notes 22 prior 10%+ corrections since 1980 averaged a 4% gain over the next 3 months, rising 73% of the time. Valuation has partly reset (forward P/E down 25% YTD to 16x) but earnings built on AI capex sit about 25% above trend, so a downside scenario (17x on trend EPS) implies 5,800 while recovery to the 10-year average P/E implies a new high of 8,100. The selloff, initially concentrated in AI stocks (GS AI basket -32% since the high), broadened this week as cyclicals underperformed defensives and the ex-AI market fell too, which Goldman reads as a growth scare, not just an AI unwind. It argues a bottom needs one of three catalysts: renewed AI-earnings confidence, a dovish Fed signal, or a sharp positioning washout. Despite hedge fund deleveraging, its Sentiment Indicator still shows elevated broad positioning, so the third condition is not yet met. Recommends defensives and buyback-heavy names; a quarterly holdings review lists eight hedge-fund/mutual-fund "shared favorite" stocks.
